entries.title: Keep bounded role work inside the coordinator task
entries.summary: For bounded role handoffs that should return automatically and let Mog continue the workflow, use internal subagents inside the main Codex task. Keep the canonical Work Item, claim, exact revision, and evidence in the repository; reserve separate user-owned Codex tasks for genuinely independent work the user needs to revisit directly. Temple currently requires an ordinary claim for sequential internal-subagent work because parallel prepare only dispatches safe parallel waves.

entries.title: Dispatch role work through coordinator-owned subagents
entries.summary: Mog keeps the main task as coordinator, gives each internal subagent one Position, Work Item, exact revision, claim, bounded paths, stop conditions, and evidence requirements, and avoids concurrent edits to the same scope. After the subagent returns, Mog verifies canonical repository state before dispatching the next Position. Use a separate user-owned Codex task only when independent user follow-up is itself required.

entries.title: Task registration does not guarantee live Token observation
entries.summary: A one-turn Codex task was registered and history-correlated to its Work Item, Position, thread, and revision, but live attachment returned thread-resume-invalid and no thread/tokenUsage/updated event was captured. Future baselines must establish observer readiness or a provider-owned launch before work begins, and missing usage must remain unknown rather than zero.

entries.title: Validate external wire contracts before live integration
entries.summary: Before the first live external-service call, inspect current official documentation and the exact installed schema or discovery endpoint, define explicit internal-to-wire mappings, and test emitted requests against that independently recorded contract. Mocks that repeat implementation assumptions do not prove compatibility; unsupported values must fail before provider contact and protocol drift must not trigger automatic retries.

entries.title: Repair explicit acceptance contracts before bounded model escalation
entries.summary: In the two corrected low-risk bounded implementation cases from WI-0132, explicit identity, immutability, idempotency, compatibility, and error semantics let Terra medium match the higher routes on objective correctness. Treat contract repair as the first diagnostic step before escalation; this low-confidence result must be revalidated on broader task families.

entries.title: Global experiment stops can erase comparative coverage
entries.summary: In Temple quote-shipping comparisons WI-0236 and WI-0239, a stopped subject prevented later cells from being observed. Review stop causes and missing-treatment coverage before another run; never bypass uncertain usage, cleanup or source validity. WI-0234 completed all cells, so the lesson is conditional, not a prohibition on shared stops.

entries.title: Reuse historical experiment evidence without pooling incompatible results
entries.summary: The quote-shipping studies retain usable ordinary and Temple product, usage and timing evidence despite later reporting and oracle changes. Inventory task seeds and each measurement contract before rerunning controls; use historical references with explicit limits, preserve original failed scores, and record offline rechecks separately. New compact behavior still requires a new observation.

entries.title: Plan incremental experiments from retained evidence
entries.summary: For Temple quote-shipping experiment design, first read the WI-0240 inventory and plan: classify reusable historical references versus missing or censored evidence; verify pre-work seed, model/runtime, prompt and acceptance compatibility; name the decision each new subject can change; review shared-stop and missing-treatment coverage offline. Prefer measuring the missing treatment to automatically rerunning every control. Preserve unknown accounting and cleanup stops. This project guidance grants no live execution authority and must be reconsidered when the task, provider or measurement contract changes.
